items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: And like Sonny Rollins when he made that couple of trio albums there, I mean you were sitting right there for a dollar and a half.

ctx.x: In New York what was 52nd Street like when you were there?

It was very easy — it had access, you could go in and out of all the clubs. Like I used to pay a dollar and a half and go in and sit in the peanut gallery in Birdland. You didn’t have to buy a drink. The peanut gallery was an area to the left of the bandstand where if you didn’t want to drink, you just wanted to hear the music, you paid your dollar and a half and sat there. It was the greatest seat in the house because you were right on top of the bandstand. So I used to try to get the end seat or the end block…
